title: The Puerto Rico Insurance Observatory: Puerto Rico's Cold Medicine Insurance Myth
description: Put $440 on the kitchen table: that is what Puerto Rico's healthcare system has, per person, per month, to cover everyone from the neighbor with kidney failure to the kid with severe asthma. On the mainland it barely buys a catastrophic plan. Out of that gap grew the island's most quoted cynical line, attributed to Dr. Victor Ramos: planes que solo cubren medicinas de catarro, plans that only cover cold medicine. This episode opens the Puerto Rico Insurance Observatory and reads the sworn, audited Planillas de Salud filed with the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance (OCS) and the NAIC: about $17.18 billion in 2025 premium for 2,999,355 covered lives; 61.9% of them on federally funded programs; Medicare Advantage and Platino carrying over 52% of every dollar because traditional Medicare barely exists on the island; a market of titans (MCS, MMM, Triple S, First Medical, Humana, Menonita) that still closed 2025 with a combined net loss of $19.8 million; and the number that ends the myth: a medical loss ratio of 90.2% market-wide, near 89% for Medicare and 95.8% for Plan Vital. A cold-medicine plan would run 20 to 30%. The closing question: CMS is building the 2027 rate book. What happens next year when you hand the system $430?
